section_summary.extract_value: This section details Study 1, which examined the factorial validity of the TILS scale using a sample of 570 Indian respondents. The sample was split into two subsamples for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), both of which supported the acceptable factorial structure of TILS in the Indian context.
section_summary.evidence_source:
2. Study 1: Factorial validity
Study 1 is based on a sample of 570 respondents, which was divided into two parts using systematic sampling. Even responses were part of subsample-1, and odd responses were included in subsample-2. Tables 1 and 2 provide details of the sampling technique, size, method of data collection, scales used and sampling description. The Cronbach's alpha values for subsample-1, subsample-2, and the overall sample were 0.826, 0.873, and 0.834. The acceptable Cronbach's alpha values are 0.70 and above. Thus, these values recommended adequate reliability of the data.
The first subsample was subjected to EFA using principal component analysis in SPSS statistics 21. The Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) test and Bartlett's test of sphericity were conducted to check the factorability of the data. The KMO value of sampling adequacy was 0.910. The acceptable KMO value is 0.70 and above. Also, statistically significant Bartlett's test of sphericity was reported at a 0.05 level of significance. The findings of these tests recommended the suitability of data for EFA. EFA, conducted using varimax rotation, suggested a single-factor solution, which explains 70.20% of the total variance. Table 3 illustrates factor loadings, communalities, and total variance explained by three statements of the TILS scale. CFA was then conducted on the second subsample using analysis of moment structure (AMOS) 18. The acceptable values of different estimates are Goodness-of-fit index (GFI)≥ 0.95; Comparative-fit-index (CFI)≥ 0.97; Standardised root mean residual (SRMR)≤ 0.05; and Root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA)< 0.08 (Hu andBentler, 1999). The default model of TILS showed acceptable and consistent values, GFI= 0.970, CFI= 0.982, SRMR= 0.030, and RMSEA= 0.0461. Also, the regression weights of the three scale items were 0.764, 0.780, and 0.623, respectively. Fig. 1 reports the CFA model of the TILS. Thus, the results of EFA and CFA concluded the acceptable factorial structure of TILS in the Indian context.
